pr_title: Include mod effects in values displayed by `BeatmapAttributeText`
pr_body:
closes https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/21946

Applying a mod with a difficulty change did previously not update the values displayed in BeatmapAttributeText. This attempts to work around this, by taking heavy "inspiration" from `osu.Game.Screens.Select.Details.AdvancedStats` and `osu.Game.Screens.Select.BeatmapInfoWedge`.

Now the displayed mod statistics are the same in the Beatmap details section in the select screen, and in the values in BeatmapAttributeText.

One thing to keep in mind is that Length will currently not get updated at all, but that seems to be a known restriction currently.
pr_comments: I will also say yet again that this component is getting very huge and complicated *very* quickly. Not happy to see increasing scope creep in this area from multiple directions.

> I will also say yet again that this component is getting very huge and complicated _very_ quickly. Not happy to see increasing scope creep in this area from multiple directions.

Tbh, I also do not see the nessesity of #21504, but not seeing the effects of at least all the osu!standard mods feels wierd. (Also this is a tangent, but why does hrdt not do ar11 in lazer? Is the ar increase just invisible still, as it is in stable?)

FWIW thought you should know that it also currently doesn't work as it should on converts. showing the original star rating instead of the one you are converting to.

I downloaded the beat from the website manually, and drag & dropped it into lazer, selected it, and started swapping rulesets. Everything worked as expected, and the beatmap info section agrees with my element.


The old Star Rating will stick around for a second after the ruleset is swapped, because it si being calculated in the background. When available, it will set the Star Rating (or never if you swap rulesets faster than the Star Rating can be calculated).

> Can you please retest with changes in this pr added? I see from the settings that you are using regular lazer, which still has this issue.

all good now, sorry for the troubles

regarding https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/22112#issuecomment-1377698480

My opinion as well. The selective computing suggested in discord was a nice step, but imo inadequate. I wanted to make a new global cache that just saves these things and reuses them for `BeatmapAttributeText` and `BeatmapInfoWedge`. Peppy is against that though, see this:
https://discord.com/channels/188630481301012481/188630652340404224/1061275307459481620

As for removing the comutation without adding a cache, I don't think I can have the same functionality (whilst decreasing performance impacts). At best I need to splitup the component into several smaller ones, which watch less stuff each e.g. 
- split all of the mod dependent stuff like CS, AR, HP, OD, Bpm into a seperate component (mods watch)
- split sr display into a seperate component (ruleset and difficultyCache watch)
- anything only dependent on the current beatmap will stay in `BeatmapAttriubuteText`

If you have any other suggestions, please let me know. So far it has been a whole lot of nothing, after I asked you what exactly you feel is inefficient. At least I got a small insight with your comment on the linked pr.

> I wanted to make a new global cache that just saves these things and reuses them for `BeatmapAttributeText` and `BeatmapInfoWedge`

I don't really have the mental energy to argue over this too much - especially so that I was against merging this feature from the start precisely due to the scope creep that it has provoked - but I still don't think anything global like that is necessary.

I consider this PR as-is unmergeable, as it is adding a lot of complication to everything because `BeatmapAttributeText` is trying to coordinate everything instead of modularising the value fetch logic appropriately (which, again, *doesn't require global caching*). I described [a sketch](https://discord.com/channels/188630481301012481/188630652340404224/1062444624129560706) of how I imagine this working on discord but if I were to go into any more detail than that I'd end up writing the entirety of the solution which I don't want to do right now.

[5335163](https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/21585/commits/53351635f94765789cad69d413227514b858efd2) and
[c8cf43c](https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/21585/commits/c8cf43c304cab515fbfb7e82cfa9707a1baef27c)
are my interpretation of what you linked on github. What you mean by `instead of modularising the value fetch logic appropriately` is a little unsure about. I don't know if what I did in those commits already covers that or not.

As for the commits [c8815cb](https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/21585/commits/c8815cb5b03217a61a692aee470332292ef1fe10) and [c65a1a7](https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/21585/commits/c65a1a73cab9425735c892c1abebd114ca12c96e), that is my version of reducing calculations even further.
Overall the concept is quite simple: One `BeatmapAttributeText` is in control of updating all of the values. If that 'in-control' `BeatmapAttributeText` get's disposed, another instance will take over if present or the `values` dictionary, `modSettingChangeTracker` and `preStarDifficultyCancellationSource` get disposed (and hopefully free'd).

Can I get a rereview of either the state at c8cf43c304cab515fbfb7e82cfa9707a1baef27c or the current state (difference is that the current state uses a static values array and computes values only ever once)

If you imagined something entirely differently, feel free to discard anything after c8cf43c304cab515fbfb7e82cfa9707a1baef27c if you so wish and implement the things you were talking about yourself (because I then apparently do not understand what you mean).

There are too many other contributions for me to get a thorough review on this as I consider this a low priority task. However at a very quick look at the current state I already don't think I'm going to like what is here now. The nine-something added members and +300 lines in `BeatmapAttributeText` alone tell me that this is likely not structured and modularised as I'd like to see it, and I cannot provide any better guidance without going to write this myself,  which I do not want to do at this time.

Thanks for the quick reply.
I understand and agree with your viewpoints.
I guess this is going to take a bit longer to get merged then, until you or another team member wants to and/or has time to look at this.
Still thanks a ton for being this open about this whole pr, eventhough you oppose it.
This isn't the way forward. There's just too much complexity, as has already been stated. Needs to be reapproached without changing the whole structure of the component. It should not be required.

issue_context.title: `BeatmapAttributeText` are not affected by mods
issue_context.body:
### Type

Cosmetic

### Bug description

As you can see from the screenshot below, `BeatmapAttributeText`s display missmatched information when adding a difficulty increasing mod. In the screenshot you can see the missmatch with AR, CS and OD.
It may be intended. 
I'm not giving attaching logs since I am importing beatmaps and they are ~20MB.

### Screenshots or videos

![osu_2022-12-30_14-52-00](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/31241607/210077550-f69aa33f-c02c-4d6c-8266-a2b8ed690c72.jpg)


### Version

2022.1228.0-lazer

### Logs

-
comments:
This can't be as hard to fix as it has been made to look in the last attempted PR.

Put another way, if it is that complex, we've done stuff very wrong.

Still experiencing this after a year. Any fix coming soon?

This is not only for difficulty increasing mods but any mod that changes the star rating.
From my knowledge the only value affected by this is the star rating attribute.
